tax.text: Aderholt says he favors targeted spending cuts over raising taxes to address the fiscal crisis.
tax.quote: I believe that targeted spending cuts are the most responsible way to address the fiscal crisis facing our country, not increasing taxes on families and small businesses.

safety.text: Aderholt says high-crime areas need a greater law-enforcement presence while also supporting training and de-escalation reforms.
safety.quote: The bottom line is this: high-crime areas need more law enforcement presence, not less; defunded police departments would make our streets more dangerous, not less; and the brave men and women who keep us safe deserve more respect, not less.

immigration.text: Aderholt calls for securing the border first and opposes automatic amnesty for those in the country illegally.
immigration.quote: I feel very strongly that amnesty should not be automatically granted to those who are here illegally.

guns.text: Aderholt says he supports expanding the rights of gun owners rather than imposing new restrictions.
guns.quote: we need to expand the rights of gun owners rather than seeking new ways to impose restrictions

abortion.text: Aderholt says he wholeheartedly believes the country should look for ways to curb and stop abortions.
abortion.quote: I also wholeheartedly believe that we should look for ways to curb and stop abortions in the United States.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: As House Values Action Team chairman, Aderholt backed the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act to restrict girls' sports to female athletes.
gender.quote: This is about protecting opportunities for female athletes to compete, succeed, and excel, as intended when Title IX was enacted.

health.text: Aderholt says he opposed the Affordable Care Act and warns that government interference raises prices.
health.quote: I opposed the President's healthcare bill, the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA), also known as Obamacare.

energy.text: Aderholt calls for increasing domestic oil, gas and coal production and opposes cap-and-trade carbon controls.
energy.quote: I certainly oppose policy proposals such as Cap & Trade and other similar carbon emission control systems that harm economic growth

voting.text: Aderholt urged passage of the SAVE Act, which adds citizenship and identification requirements to federal voting procedures.
voting.quote: We need to restore confidence in our voters and integrity in our elections, because it’s common sense that American elections should be decided by American voters, and American voters only.

wages.text: Pusczek calls for a $15 federal minimum wage indexed to cost of living and for passing the PRO Act to strengthen unions.
wages.quote: Champions legislation to immediately raise the federal minimum wage to $15.00 per hour, tying future increases to regional cost-of-living and inflation indexes.

debt.text: Her platform calls for strengthening Social Security without cuts and protecting and expanding Medicare.
debt.quote: defending and strengthening Social Security with no cuts—ever

schools.text: She supports increased investment in public schools and opposes diverting public funds to private and charter schools.
schools.quote: Protecting Public Education from Privatization by opposing the diversion of public funds to private and charter schools

immigration.text: Her immigration platform calls for speeding up legal immigration and naturalization while keeping families together.
immigration.quote: accelerating the legal immigration and naturalization process by increasing judge appointments to address COVID era backlogs, prioritizing keeping families together and ending cruel separations

abortion.text: She cited Alabama’s restrictions on reproductive rights as a reason for running for Congress.
abortion.quote: She cites Alabama’s ‘growing restrictions on healthcare and reproductive rights that make it nearly impossible for her and Trever to start the family they dreamed of,’ a driving force in her decision to seek the Democratic nomination for Alabama’s Fourth Congressional District.

health.text: She would let the federal government directly enroll low-income people in non-expansion states into public coverage, bypassing state governments.
health.quote: Introduces legislation enabling the federal government to directly enroll eligible low-income individuals in non-expansion states into local managed-care plans or a federal insurance pool, completely bypassing obstructionist state governments.
